rationale: The anaesthesia chief's concern is supported: charts record nausea severity and mobilisation poorly (c2), and a nurse-led readiness assessment captures them well (c6). A 12-month prospective cohort would measure these variables directly and could build on published predictors (c1).
alternatives: Retrospective chart review of 2019 to 2025 procedures (not preferred: charts miss nausea severity and mobilisation)
Adopt the published nine-predictor model (refused: not validated)
whyNotMoreComplex: A multi-hospital prospective study would add generalisability the unit does not need.

decision.statement: Collect a prospective cohort of all elective laparoscopic cholecystectomies for 12 months from January 2027 with a standard nurse-led discharge readiness assessment at four hours, recording nausea severity and the time of first walking, and develop a booking-time prediction model from it.
decision.question: Which data should the booking-time prediction model be built on?

criteria.text: Charts miss nausea severity and mobilisation times, which a prospective assessment would capture.
The prospective cohort gives too few events to develop and validate a model within the time available.

gates.requirement: Nursing time to run the readiness assessment for 12 months
Analyst time for data management and modelling
gates.evidence: Decision support request DS-2026-88 for about 20 analyst days, supplied by the investigator

alternatives: Retrospective chart review of 2019 to 2025 procedures
decision.note: Rests on claims c1, c2 and c6; the nursing gate has no evidence.

summary: Prospective cohort recommended; blocked until nursing time is found.
